immutable_failure_reproduction.root_cause: 1. GET /bff/personas relied on _list_persona_records which only merged read_store and _PERSONA_BFF_OVERLAY; on process restart, _PERSONA_BFF_OVERLAY was wiped and PersonaProvisioningStore was not queried for tenant-scoped list records. 2. PersonaProvisioningStore lacked list_by_tenant and list_all methods on the protocol, Memory store, and Postgres store. 3. Detail readback in bff_get_persona swallowed provisioning store exceptions and raised a false 404 rather than failing closed with a typed 503 DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE error. 4. Prior evidence manifest misattributed workflow 33291750319 directly to merge e7f010dc and listed a pre-workflow commit SHA (2f741da8dfb3b802613cfcf55e3e2cbe826dbbb5) with a typo in unblocks_task.

reviewer_findings: Restart regressions instantiated a fresh MemoryPersonaProvisioningStore and then wrote its private _records/_names/_personas fields directly (plus a private _copy call) instead of proving two identity-distinct public-protocol store instances read one shared durable backend.

_list_persona_records() defaulted an absent tenant to store.list_all(), so GET /bff/search (and other unscoped callers) leaked a Persona reserved under another tenant to an authenticated caller (proven with persona-cross-tenant-durable-canary via GET /bff/search as op-2:operator).

Two of the three commits on the branch (962a881d8, 1faa11543) used a conventional-commit subject ("fix(bff): ...") instead of the required "<TASK-ID>: <summary>" prefix, failing the required Commit trailers check across the whole PR range.
repair_this_round: Added MemoryProvisioningBackend, a shared durable-state object; MemoryPersonaProvisioningStore(backend=...) lets a second identity-distinct store instance read the same backing state through only the public reserve/get/list_by_tenant/list_all/acquire/checkpoint/release protocol. The three restart tests now construct fresh_store = MemoryPersonaProvisioningStore(backend=store.backend) and assert fresh_store is not store, with no private-field writes anywhere in the test file.

_list_persona_records, _pm12_persona_league_rows, _persona_intent_all_items, and _health_reason_sentinel_findings now take an explicit tenant_id and every authenticated user-facing caller (GET /bff/search, the persona-league family, GET /bff/management/persona-intent, GET /bff/v5/sentinel/findings, and the management NL assistant) derives the caller's own tenant via _bff_me_tenant_payload and passes it through, instead of defaulting to list_all(). Fixed a related latent bug in _bff_me_tenant_payload where its default-tenant claim lookup only checked singular tenant_id/tenantId claim keys, not the plural tenant_ids/tenantIds keys already used for allowed-tenant validation, which could route a caller's default tenant to the wrong value. Added four negative regressions (search, persona-league, persona-intent, sentinel/findings) that reserve a Persona under tenant-other directly via the store and assert it never appears in a tenant-dev caller's response.

The recovered implementation is ready to be carried by clean task-scoped history. The existing remote PR #5427 still contains the two earlier non-compliant commit subjects cited above, so it is not evidence of an approvable delivery and must not be merged without an authorized clean-history recovery.
